public_rationale: Primary sources document real non-AI GPU uses, including molecular dynamics and cryptography. These qualify the argument but do not disprove a claim that alternative uses are few or commercially small. The available evidence does not establish their revenue at hyperscale deployment levels. Neither technical versatility alone nor missing revenue disclosures settles the compound claim.
limitations: The examples are not a comprehensive workload survey.
A technical application can be useful without supporting substantial commercial demand.
The result depends partly on undefined scope and scale terms.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI data center GPUs have very few use cases outside AI, none of which drive hyperscale revenue, unlike fiber.

statement.excerpt: AI data centers are nothing like fiber, because there are very few actual use cases for these GPUs outside of AI, and none of them are remotely hyperscale revenue drivers.

from_speaker: none of them are remotely hyperscale revenue drivers
our_interpretation: These GPUs means the accelerator hardware used in AI data centers, rather than every consumer graphics card.
The ordinary reading is that practical alternative workloads are limited and cannot provide commercial demand on the scale motivating hyperscale AI infrastructure.
Assess the current quarter through the day before publication, July 1 through September 28, 2025, as the latest reportable interval for the ongoing capability and market claim.
Treat the fiber comparison as the implication of the stated workload and commercial-scale claims, rather than a claim that the technologies have no similarities.
No particular company’s financial metric is asserted, so metric_scope is null. No arbitrary revenue threshold is added.
criteria.support_condition: Broad evidence shows a narrow set of practical non-AI workloads on the relevant GPUs and commercial demand too small to sustain comparable hyperscale deployment.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishes a broad practical non-AI workload base, or a non-AI workload producing commercial demand at comparable hyperscale deployment levels on the relevant GPUs.

evidence.explanation: The benchmark documents molecular dynamics simulations on an AI-relevant GPU. It predates the target period and does not establish the number or commercial scale of alternative workloads.
GPU cryptography is a documented non-AI application. Its existence alone neither disproves very few use cases nor establishes hyperscale revenue.
